# Agent Admin API

The Shipwright admin service exposes a CRUD API for managing agents and their resources. It is the control plane used by the admin UI, the [`agent-admin`](https://github.com/app-vitals/shipwright/blob/main/plugins/shipwright/skills/agent-admin/SKILL.md) skill, and the provisioning pipeline.

Base path: `/agents`

**Full endpoint reference** — every route, parameter, request/response shape, and status code — lives in the generated [`admin/openapi.json`](../admin/openapi.json) spec. **Practical usage** — curl-based examples for common agent-management calls — lives in the [`agent-admin`](https://github.com/app-vitals/shipwright/blob/main/plugins/shipwright/skills/agent-admin/SKILL.md) skill.

This page covers only the auth model and behavioral nuance the spec doesn't carry. Cron jobs and cron runs are documented in [`docs/agent-api-ops.md`](./agent-api-ops.md). The allowed-tools list, API tokens, plugins, chat token usage, and the GitHub installations snapshot are documented in [`docs/agent-api-resources.md`](./agent-api-resources.md).

---

## Authentication

Three auth paths are checked in order:

1. **Admin key** — `Authorization: Bearer <key>` where the key matches an entry in `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_API_KEYS`. Sets `isAdmin=true`, bypasses all per-agent checks.
2. **Per-agent bearer token** — `Authorization: Bearer <token>` where the token is a per-agent DB token scoped to a specific agent ID. Sets `isAdmin=false`, restricts access to that agent's own routes (`403` on cross-agent access).
3. **Session cookie** — `admin_session` httpOnly JWT verified with `SHIPWRIGHT_SESSION_SECRET`. `isAdmin` comes from the JWT's `isAdmin` claim (see [Session cookies](#session-cookies)).

If an `Authorization` header is present but the token is invalid in both token paths, the request is rejected with `401` (no fallthrough to cookie). Missing auth returns `401`. Cross-agent access with a per-agent token returns `403`.

Routes marked **admin-only** in the OpenAPI spec require `isAdmin=true`. Per-agent bearer tokens cannot call these routes.

Every `/agents/*` (and `/accounts/*`) route sits behind one auth middleware
(`admin/src/api-auth.ts`). It accepts a bearer token or, when no `Authorization`
header is sent, a session cookie. A present-but-invalid bearer is a 401 and
never falls through to the cookie.

### Bearer scope kinds

`SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_API_KEYS` is a comma-separated list of `name:token:scope`
entries. The middleware exposes the result as `scope: {kind, agentId?}` beside
`isAdmin` and `caller` (and `callerLabel()` includes the kind in log lines).

| Scope in the key | Kind | `isAdmin` | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| `*` | `admin` | true | Everything. |
| `<agentId>` (or a DB agent token) | `agent` | false | Routes of that one agent. |
| `platform.read` | `platform-read` | false | Every `GET`/`HEAD`; every mutating method is 403. |
| `platform.ops` | `platform-ops` | false | Everything `platform.read` has, plus the mutating routes in `PLATFORM_OPS_ROUTES`. |
| _(none, session cookie)_ | _(no `scope`)_ | per the JWT's `isAdmin` claim | Not a key scope: a cookie sets `caller.scope` to `session` for logging only. See [Session cookies](#session-cookies). |

`PLATFORM_OPS_ROUTES` (exported from `api-auth.ts`) is the complete list of
mutating routes a `platform.ops` key may call:

| Method | Path | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `PATCH` | `/agents/{id}` | Any field except `accountId`, which stays platform-admin only. |
| `POST` | `/agents/{id}/repos` | Also matches deeper paths. |
| `DELETE` | `/agents/{id}/repos` | Also matches deeper paths, e.g. `/agents/{id}/repos/{owner}/{name}`. |
| `PATCH` | `/agents/{id}/crons/{cronId}` | |
| `POST` | `/agents/{id}/ask` | Flag-gated, see [Security posture](#security-posture). |
| `POST` | `/agents/{id}/chat-credentials` | Also matches deeper paths. Flag-gated. |
| `DELETE` | `/agents/{id}/chat-credentials` | Also matches deeper paths, e.g. `/agents/{id}/chat-credentials/{tokenId}`. Flag-gated. |

Every other mutating route (env writes, agent create/delete/provision, tokens,
federation, accounts) stays 403 for both platform scopes.

`AGENT_CROSS_ROUTES` (`POST /agents/{id}/ask`) is the one route an `<agentId>`
key may call on another agent's path; see [Security posture](#security-posture).

#### The colon rule

`parseAdminApiKeys` takes the **last** colon-separated segment as the scope and
everything between the name and the scope as the token. A colon inside a scope
name would therefore be read as part of the token, so scopes never contain one;
that is why the platform scopes are dot-spelled (`platform.read`, not
`platform:read`).

### Security posture

The ask, chat-credential and `/doc` surfaces are opt-in and fail closed:

- **Off by default, 404 when off.** `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_ASK_ENABLED` (plus `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_ASK_ALLOWLIST`), `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_TOKEN_MINT_ENABLED` and `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_DOC_ENABLED` each enable their routes only when set to the literal `enabled` (see [configuration-agent.md](configuration-agent.md)). Otherwise the routes answer `404` (`/doc` is not mounted at all), so a caller cannot tell them from a build without the feature.
- **Self-serve is the same kind of flag.** `SHIPWRIGHT_SELF_SERVE_ENABLED` gates account-user agent creation and account-based caller scope the same way (see [self-serve.md](self-serve.md)).
- **Server-set ask authority.** `POST /agents/{id}/ask` accepts `*`, `platform.ops`, or the `<agentId>` key whose agent equals the body's `from`. An agent key may reach another agent's `/ask` path but only as itself; the server compares `from` to the key's agent and any mismatch is a `403`. The `from>to` pair must also be on `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_ASK_ALLOWLIST` (empty denies all).
- **Depth 1.** An ask always creates a thread with `askDepth: 1`; any other `depth` is a `400`, so an asked agent cannot chain further asks.
- **Audit row.** Every ask writes an `AgentAsk` row (agents, thread, depth, wait, status, caller label) and never stores or logs the question text.
- **Raw tokens returned once.** `POST /agents/{id}/chat-credentials` returns `rawToken` only in the create response; admin neither stores nor logs it, and the list route returns no raw values. Chat credentials are never mintable by the agent's own key, and the body cannot name a different `agentId`.

### Session cookies

The cookie is a JWT. `isAdmin` comes from the JWT's `isAdmin` claim (a missing
or non-true claim is non-admin), not from the presence of a cookie. Non-admin
cookies reach `GET /agents` (filtered to their memberships) and
`/agents/{id}/**` for agents they are members of; everything else is 403.
Cookies do not set `scope`.

## Agents

`GET`/`POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE /agents[/:id]`, `POST /agents/:id/provision`, and `POST /agents/reconcile` are fully described in the OpenAPI spec — including the rollback-guarded provisioning block. Field semantics the spec doesn't carry:

`POST /agents` requires either an admin key, a session cookie, or account membership (SSP-4.2). Per-agent bearer tokens cannot call it. **Platform admins** (admin key or session cookie with `isAdmin=true`) keep today's behavior — unrestricted specialty, optional accountId, and unassigned agents (where accountId is null). **Account users** — non-admins authenticated via session cookie with an account membership — may create agents in their own account only: the accountId is resolved from their scope (not the request body), the specialty is forced to `"coding"` (SELF_SERVE_AGENT_TYPE), and `403` is returned if they have no account. **Owner (PAI-1.2):** the created agent's `ownerEmail` is the authenticated caller's lower-cased email — the session user, or a bearer admin key whose name is itself a valid email address; otherwise it is left unset. A client-supplied `ownerEmail` in the body is ignored. The route shares its implementation with the web UI form at `/admin/agents/new`: both call the same `createAgent()` function (`admin/src/agents.ts`), which validates name/typeName, creates the Agent row, seeds AgentTool/AgentPlugin rows from the selected Specialty manifest (member emails and repos come from their own dedicated fields, not the manifest — no Specialty shipped today populates a `members`/`repos` array), and (for non-self-hosted agents) provisions the Kubernetes workload. The request body takes the same raw, unparsed fields the form submits (e.g. newline-separated `reposRaw`/`authorAllowlistRaw`); creation is transactional — any failure (missing fields, unresolvable `typeName`, malformed repo/allowlist lines, provisioning failure, account quota exceeded, account inactive or not found) leaves zero rows behind rather than a partial-success 200. **Account status and quota:** when an agent is created with an accountId — either by an admin supply or by an account user (SSP-4.2) — the account's status and `maxAgents` quota are enforced: an `inactive` or nonexistent account returns `account_inactive`; an active account at or above its `maxAgents` limit returns `quota_exceeded`. Both checks are race-safe via database locks (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) inside the creation transaction. A `repos` list containing two repos with the same basename under different owners (e.g. `a/app` and `b/app`) is rejected with `400` and a message naming the colliding pair, because the agent's `repos/<name>` clone folders are keyed by basename; the same check applies to repo-scope edits on the agent detail page. See the [`agent-admin`](https://github.com/app-vitals/shipwright/blob/main/plugins/shipwright/skills/agent-admin/SKILL.md) skill for the walkthrough.

- **`reviewAuthorAllowlist`** vs **`patchAuthorAllowlist`** are not symmetric: an empty `reviewAuthorAllowlist` means "all authenticated users" (fail-open), while an empty `patchAuthorAllowlist` means "self-authored PRs only" — `patchAuthorAllowlist` is additive on top of that, enforced at runtime by ``check-patch` in the shipwright coding runtime`, which merges allowlisted-author PRs into the self-authored candidate pool and deduplicates by `(repo, PR number)`.
- **`GET /agents/:id`** returns the owner and Anthropic identity (PAI-2.5): `ownerEmail`, `anthropicIdentityName`, `anthropicServiceAccountId` (the `svac_…` ID) and `anthropicFederationRuleId` (the `fdrl_…` ID), each `null` when unset, so an agent can be traced to its Anthropic identity. The list route (`GET /agents`) omits them, and `k8sServiceAccountName` is never part of the response.
- **`slackId`** is normally resolved and persisted automatically via `auth.test` right after Slack OAuth completes; it's directly settable only to backfill it for agents that connected Slack before that fix shipped.
- **`DELETE /agents/:id`**'s `manualStepsRequired` response entries flag state with no automated revocation path: hand-pasted secrets (`GH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, and any other `AgentEnv` row with `secret: true`) must be revoked by hand at their respective provider, plus a Slack-app entry when `SLACK_APP_ID` is set but no `xoxpToken` was supplied to the delete call. When automated removal of a per-agent Anthropic identity fails, the entries also name each identity piece still live (federation rule, Anthropic service account, Kubernetes ServiceAccount) to archive or delete by hand.

## Environment variables

Env vars are stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM) and decrypted on read. `POST /agents/:id/envs` bulk-replaces every env var; `PATCH /agents/:id/envs` updates specific keys without touching others.

When Anthropic workload identity federation is enabled (provisioning on and either `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_IDENTITY_MODE` set to `perAgent`, or `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID` set in the default `shared` mode), `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` are blocked for non-self-hosted agents, because each outranks federation in the Anthropic client even when empty. `POST`/`PATCH /agents/:id/envs`, the admin UI env editor, `POST /agents` (`claudeCodeOauthToken` / `anthropicApiKey`) and Slack/GitHub provisioning reject them with a `400` whose body carries `code: "anthropic_credentials_blocked_federation"`. `GET /agents/:id/config` strips the three keys from the bundle (logging the agent ID and key names, never values), and the agent itself skips them and deletes them from `process.env` when `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID` is in its pod env. Self-hosted agents and deployments without federation are unchanged.

**Migrating existing agents (`POST /agents/federation/strip-credentials`).** The guards above keep the three keys from reaching agents, but bundles saved before federation was enabled still store them. This admin-only, one-off endpoint deletes `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` from every non-self-hosted agent's bundle and returns `{ dryRun, agents: [{ agentId, keys }] }` (key names only, never values; agents without any of the keys are omitted).

1. Dry run: `POST /agents/federation/strip-credentials` (`dryRun` defaults to `true`) and review the list.
2. Apply: `POST /agents/federation/strip-credentials?dryRun=false`. A second call returns an empty `agents` list.
3. Restart the affected agents so running pods drop the keys from their environment.
4. Verify with `GET /agents/:id/envs` that none of the three keys remain.

Self-hosted agents and all other keys are untouched.

## Runtime config

```
GET /agents/:id/config
```

Polled by the agent harness on startup and during its config sync loop — the one route on this page the harness itself calls, as opposed to the admin UI or provisioning pipeline. Returns the full config bundle: decrypted env vars, allowed-tools patterns, installed plugins, scoped repos, `reviewAuthorAllowlist`/`patchAuthorAllowlist`/`restrictSlackToMembers`, `phaseMethodology` (map of phase names to subagent-type overrides, with defaults filled in for phases not explicitly overridden), derived `memberEmails` (empty unless `restrictSlackToMembers` is `true` and members are configured), and **APM-1.5:** the six agent-policy fields (`autoPostReviews`, `allowSelfReview`, `minConfidence`, `maxFindings`, `cleanupMergedWorktrees`, `cleanupAfterDays`) for direct passthrough to the runtime. Returns `404` if the agent doesn't exist.
